_doc: WP-Q8: layouts of world-kit pieces (world_kits.py). Blender frame, metres: x right, y forward, z up. A Quaternius wall module is 2 m wide and looks to -Y at yaw 0; `ring` turns every side's front inward, so a camera at -Y sees the north wall's face. Block types: ring (nx*ny modules of `wall` on the rectangle centre line, `replace` {side:i -> asset}, `open_sides`, `corner`), floor (nx*ny tiles), row (one asset repeated every `step` m from `from` to `to`), piece (one placement). The same layout is reused by any number of shots; `landmarks` name pieces the scene_set marks.

castle_courtyard.label: A walled castle courtyard, 8 x 6 m, south side open for the camera, a gate and a fort behind it

village_street.label: A plaster village street, a row of house fronts on each side

hill_castle.label: A castle on a hill above a walled-bridge river and a plaster town, pines and broadleaf trees, mountains behind

antique_forum.label: E1 Antiquity: a Greco-Roman forum in front of a columned temple, statues, market stalls and a crowd

harbour_square.label: E3 Early modern: a harbour town square, timber-and-plaster houses, stalls, barrels, a pier and Dutch ships

field_camp.label: E4 Nineteenth century: a field camp, canvas tents, wagons, lamps and a campfire, pines and mountains behind
